entries.question: When is graph structure worth its cost in retrieval-augmented generation?
entries.note: Retrieval correctly surfaces the right document (verified: it supplies 4 of the raw top-5 nearest neighbors). But its own two lowest-distance chunks are the paper's title/abstract line (near-verbatim overlap with the query's own phrasing), not the conclusion section that actually states the paper's answer -- that chunk exists in the document but ranks 4th by distance, so select_context_chunks's per-document cap (top-2 by distance at the time) excludes it. gpt-4.1-nano correctly refuses given only the abstract-restating chunks it actually receives (verified 3/3, forced model=gpt-4.1-nano, 2026-09-18) -- a real chunk-quality gap (boilerplate/title text outranking substantive content by raw embedding distance), not a retrieval or selection defect. Originally written expecting 'supported'; corrected after live verification rather than guessed, matching this project's never-guess discipline. Underlying document (arxiv-2609.18099-when-is-graph-structure-worth-its-cost-rag) is one of the 31 survivors of the 700KB-cap expansion, still valid as of 2026-09-19.
